name: Tyson Foods, Inc.

opportunitySignals.message: Phase tracker reads structural pivot in progress (P8 · PIVOT) with composite=0.310 stable below distress threshold. Capital-allocation target if narrative supports turnaround thesis. Pair with management-change tracker.

domainRelevance: Tyson Foods is the largest U.S. meat processor by volume, controlling ~20% of U.S. chicken production, ~15% of beef, and ~10% of pork. The company operates a vertically integrated supply chain from animal genetics and feed mills through primary processing to branded consumer products (Hillshire Farm, Jimmy Dean, Ball Park). Tyson's scale and commodity-price exposure make it a critical node in the food-supply-chain network, with direct leverage over retail and foodservice pricing.
portalRelevance: Tyson is a Tier-1 supply-chain anchor in the Walmart functional network, serving as both a primary supplier to major retailers and foodservice operators and a bellwether for commodity-input inflation (corn, soybean meal, natural gas). The company's financial health and operational capacity directly signal downstream food-price inflation and retail-margin compression; its debt trajectory and free-cash-flow generation are leading indicators of working-capital stress in the broader food-supply ecosystem.

notes.cohortStatus: S&P 500 constituent; Tyson family retains ~71% voting control via Class B shares

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Weekly live-animal procurement prices (cattle, hog, broiler) vs. forward commodity curves
8-K filings for plant closures, recalls, or major customer contract wins/losses
Quarterly gross-margin variance decomposition (input cost vs. selling-price realization)
USDA FSIS inspection reports and recall announcements affecting production capacity

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Phase classification (P8 PIVOT stable; monitor for P9 inflection if debt/EBITDA exceeds 3.5x)
Rolling 4-quarter free-cash-flow trajectory and working-capital swing (inventory + receivables)
Capacity utilization by segment (poultry, beef, pork) vs. historical 85–92% baseline
Debt maturity ladder and refinancing risk; next major bond maturity Q3 2027

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Pattern match: commodity-input spike (corn >$5.50/bu, soy >$12/bu) triggers 60–90 day margin compression before pricing power materializes
Retail customer concentration risk: Walmart + top-5 customers represent ~35% of revenue; loss of major account triggers 8–12% EBITDA shock
Foodservice recovery trajectory post-2024 inflation; QSR chicken demand elasticity vs. beef/pork substitution
Regulatory distress signature: OSHA citations + USDA recall frequency as leading indicator of operational stress

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Commodity-input hedge: long corn/soy futures when TSN margin-to-input ratio falls below 15%; unwind on realization
Debt-service coverage monitoring: if FCF/debt-service falls below 1.3x, trigger capital-allocation pause (buyback suspension)
Customer concentration mitigation: track new QSR/foodservice wins; model revenue impact of top-5 customer loss scenario
Environmental/OSHA compliance cost accrual: EPA water-discharge permits + OSHA workplace-safety citations as drag on FCF

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Long TSN equity if P8 PIVOT narrative confirmed by management guidance + debt reduction roadmap in next earnings call
Short TSN if live-animal procurement costs spike >20% YoY without corresponding retail price realization within 60 days
Pair trade: long TSN / short WMT if Tyson margin compression signals broader retail-supply-chain stress
Hedge via long corn/soy calls if TSN guidance implies input-cost pass-through risk; unwind on Q+1 earnings beat

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q+1 earnings: validate gross-margin recovery vs. commodity-input baseline; track customer pricing realization
Stock price reaction to earnings: >5% move signals market repricing of pivot thesis; <2% suggests thesis still embedded
10-Q working-capital disclosure: inventory days outstanding (DIO) and accounts-payable days (DPO) signal supply-chain stress
Debt covenant compliance: monitor leverage ratio (net debt/EBITDA) vs. 3.5x covenant threshold; early warning if trending >3.2x

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Reweight commodity-input sensitivity: if corn volatility (VIX-style measure) increases, increase hedge ratio from 40% to 60% of forward exposure
Recalibrate customer-concentration risk: if Walmart share of revenue falls below 18%, reduce concentration-loss scenario severity
Update phase-transition thresholds: if P8 PIVOT persists >4 quarters without P9 inflection, extend pivot window or flag model drift
Incorporate ESG/regulatory tail risk: if OSHA/EPA enforcement intensity increases, add 50–100 bps to cost-of-capital assumption

functionalNetwork.model: Tyson Foods operates as a distributed processing and distribution network with three primary functional clusters: (1) upstream animal-genetics and feed-mill operations (sensory input layer); (2) primary processing plants and production scheduling (motor/striatal operations); (3) downstream branded-product distribution and customer-relationship management (salience and reward-prediction layer). The company's financial health is a function of commodity-input volatility (corn, soy, energy), customer concentration risk (Walmart, McDonald's, Yum! Brands), and regulatory compliance burden (USDA, EPA, OSHA). Tyson's debt load ($8.1B) and modest cash position ($500M) create a tight working-capital constraint that amplifies the impact of input-cost shocks and customer-demand swings.

suppliers.name: Archer-Daniels-Midland Company
suppliers.brainNodeRole: Raw Materials — corn and soybean meal
suppliers.relationshipNote: ADM supplies ~15–20% of Tyson's animal-feed inputs (corn, soybean meal, vitamin/mineral premixes). ADM also competes with Tyson's own feed division (Tyson Animal Nutrition), creating a dual supplier-competitor dynamic. Tyson's feed mills process ADM commodities into finished rations; ADM's pricing power directly flows through to Tyson's COGS.

suppliers.name: Bunge Global SA
suppliers.relationshipNote: Bunge supplies soybean meal, canola meal, and protein concentrates to Tyson feed mills. Bunge's oilseed-processing capacity in the U.S. Midwest is a critical diversification source vs. ADM; Tyson maintains dual sourcing to mitigate single-supplier risk. Bunge's margin compression in 2024–25 has reduced competitive pricing pressure on Tyson's feed division.

suppliers.name: Darling Ingredients Inc.
suppliers.brainNodeRole: Raw Materials — rendered animal proteins and fats
suppliers.relationshipNote: Darling supplies rendered animal proteins (meat and bone meal, poultry by-products) and fats to Tyson feed mills. Darling's rendering operations are vertically integrated with Tyson's own processing plants; Tyson sells offal and trim to Darling, which renders it back into feed ingredients. This closed-loop recycling reduces Tyson's net feed-input cost by ~2–3% annually.

suppliers.name: Alltech, Inc.
suppliers.brainNodeRole: Information Flow — feed additives and probiotics
suppliers.relationshipNote: Alltech supplies specialty feed additives (probiotics, enzymes, mycotoxin binders) to Tyson's feed mills. Alltech's products support Tyson's "no antibiotics ever" (NAE) positioning, which is a key differentiator for Walmart and other major retailers. Alltech's pricing power has increased as NAE demand has grown; estimated 3–5% of Tyson's feed-mill COGS.

suppliers.name: Perdue Agribusiness
suppliers.brainNodeRole: Raw Materials — live broiler chicks and genetics
suppliers.relationshipNote: Perdue Agribusiness supplies broiler chicks and genetic lines to Tyson's poultry operations. Perdue's breeding programs have improved feed-conversion efficiency and meat yield; Tyson's reliance on Perdue genetics creates a supplier-dependency risk.

suppliers.name: Elanco Animal Health Inc.
suppliers.brainNodeRole: Information Flow — animal-health pharmaceuticals and vaccines
suppliers.relationshipNote: Elanco supplies vaccines, antibiotics (for therapeutic use), and growth-promoting additives to Tyson's animal-health programs. Elanco's market share in poultry vaccines has grown as Tyson has shifted toward NAE production; Tyson's adoption of Elanco's Phibro-acquired product lines (e.g., Coban for coccidiosis control) has reduced disease-related mortality by ~1–2% in broiler flocks.

suppliers.name: Packaging Corporation of America
suppliers.brainNodeRole: Operations — corrugated packaging for meat products
suppliers.relationshipNote: PKG supplies corrugated boxes and packaging materials for Tyson's branded consumer products (Hillshire Farm, Jimmy Dean). PKG's containerboard pricing is a pass-through cost; Tyson's 10-K discloses packaging as a material cost component. PKG's capacity constraints in 2024–25 have created lead-time pressure for Tyson's retail-product shipments.

suppliers.name: Sealed Air Corporation
suppliers.brainNodeRole: Operations — flexible packaging and vacuum-seal films
suppliers.relationshipNote: Sealed Air supplies vacuum-seal films, shrink-wrap, and modified-atmosphere-packaging (MAP) materials for Tyson's fresh and processed meat products. Sealed Air's proprietary MAP technology extends shelf life and reduces spoilage; Tyson's adoption of Sealed Air's solutions has reduced retail-level shrink by ~0.5–1% in key categories.

suppliers.name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services, Inc.
suppliers.brainNodeRole: Production & Delivery — refrigerated trucking and logistics
suppliers.relationshipNote: J.B. Hunt operates Tyson's largest dedicated refrigerated-trucking fleet, managing ~25–30% of Tyson's outbound shipments to retail and foodservice customers. Hunt's real-time temperature monitoring and route optimization reduce spoilage and improve on-time delivery. Tyson's 10-K discloses transportation as a material cost; Hunt's fuel-surcharge pass-through is a key margin variable.

suppliers.name: Werner Enterprises, Inc.
suppliers.brainNodeRole: Production & Delivery — refrigerated and dry-van trucking
suppliers.relationshipNote: Werner operates a secondary refrigerated-trucking contract with Tyson, handling ~10–15% of outbound shipments. Werner's lower-cost model vs. J.B. Hunt provides competitive pricing pressure; Tyson uses Werner for lower-margin, longer-haul routes to regional distribution centers.

logisticsPartners.name: Sysco Corporation
logisticsPartners.brainNodeRole: Production & Delivery — foodservice distribution and logistics
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Sysco is the largest U.S. foodservice distributor and a critical logistics partner for Tyson's foodservice-channel products. Sysco aggregates Tyson chicken, beef, and pork products into regional distribution centers and delivers to independent restaurants, hotels, and institutional accounts. Sysco's margin compression in 2024–25 has reduced its ability to absorb Tyson price increases, creating channel conflict.

logisticsPartners.name: XPO Logistics, Inc.
logisticsPartners.brainNodeRole: Production & Delivery — last-mile and regional distribution
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: XPO operates regional distribution and last-mile delivery services for Tyson's retail-channel products. XPO's network of distribution centers in major metro areas enables Tyson to reduce inventory carrying costs and improve fill rates to Walmart and other major retailers. XPO's labor-cost inflation has pressured margins; Tyson has negotiated multi-year rate locks to mitigate exposure.

customers.name: Walmart Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Walmart is Tyson's largest customer, representing ~18–20% of consolidated revenue (~$4.5–5B annually). Tyson supplies fresh chicken, beef, pork, and branded products (Hillshire Farm, Jimmy Dean) to Walmart's ~4,700 U.S. stores. Walmart's 2016 shift to "no antibiotics ever" (NAE) chicken forced Tyson to retool its poultry supply chain; Tyson now supplies 100% NAE chicken to Walmart. Walmart's pricing power and private-label expansion create ongoing margin pressure on Tyson.

customers.name: McDonald's Corporation
customers.relationshipNote: McDonald's is Tyson's second-largest customer by volume, representing ~8–10% of revenue. Tyson supplies McNuggets, McChicken patties, and breakfast sausage to ~13,000 U.S. McDonald's locations. The McNugget supply chain is a dedicated production line at Tyson's Springdale, AR facility; McDonald's demand volatility directly drives Tyson's poultry-segment utilization. McDonald's 2024 E. coli incident in lettuce created cross-contamination risk perception for Tyson suppliers.

customers.name: Yum! Brands, Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: Yum! Brands (KFC, Taco Bell, Pizza Hut) is a top-5 Tyson customer, representing ~5–7% of revenue. Tyson supplies bone-in and boneless chicken to KFC (~7,000 U.S. locations) and seasoned ground beef to Taco Bell. KFC's 2019–2023 chicken-sandwich wars drove Tyson allocation pressure and premium pricing. Yum!'s shift toward plant-based protein options (Beyond Meat partnership) creates long-term demand substitution risk for Tyson poultry.

customers.name: Costco Wholesale Corporation
customers.relationshipNote: Costco is a major retail customer for Tyson's fresh chicken and beef, representing ~3–5% of revenue. Costco's private-label (Kirkland Signature) meat products are sourced from Tyson; Costco's membership model and high-volume throughput create stable, predictable demand. Costco's pricing discipline and low-margin model limit Tyson's ability to pass through input-cost increases.

customers.name: Kroger Co.
customers.relationshipNote: Kroger is a major regional grocery customer for Tyson's fresh and processed meat products, representing ~2–4% of revenue. Kroger's private-label meat program and regional distribution create opportunities for Tyson to optimize production scheduling. Kroger's 2024 merger with Albertsons (pending FTC approval) could consolidate Tyson's customer base and increase concentration risk.

customers.name: The Kraft Heinz Company
customers.relationshipNote: Kraft Heinz is a major customer purchasing pork, beef, and chicken for Oscar Mayer, Lunchables, and Heinz-branded meat products. As a downstream demand anchor in the Walmart network, KHC's procurement volume and commodity hedging decisions directly influence Tyson's pricing power and margin realization across retail channels.

customers.name: Cargill, Incorporated
customers.brainNodeRole: Raw Materials — commodity grain and feed ingredients
customers.relationshipNote: Cargill is a major supplier of corn, soybean meal, and specialty feed additives to Tyson. As a private company, Cargill's pricing and contract terms are opaque; however, Cargill's scale in U.S. grain handling gives it significant leverage in feed-ingredient negotiations. Tyson's 10-K discloses commodity-price risk but not Cargill-specific exposure.

competitors.name: Pilgrim's Pride Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Pilgrim's Pride is the second-largest U.S. poultry processor (~15% market share vs. Tyson's ~20%). PPC is majority-owned by JBS S.A. (Brazilian beef giant), which provides capital and operational leverage. PPC and Tyson together control ~35% of U.S. chicken production; DOJ price-fixing investigation (2019–2021) targeted both companies. PPC's lower debt load ($3.2B vs. Tyson's $8.1B) provides competitive flexibility.

competitors.name: JBS S.A.
competitors.brainNodeRole: Perspective-Taking — global beef and pork competitor
competitors.relationshipNote: JBS S.A. (Brazilian multinational) is the world's largest meat processor and Tyson's primary global competitor. JBS controls Pilgrim's Pride (U.S. poultry), Seara (Brazil poultry/beef), and Friboi (Brazil beef). JBS's 2021 ransomware attack and subsequent operational disruptions created temporary market-share gains for Tyson. JBS's lower leverage and diversified geography reduce Tyson's competitive advantage in commodity-price cycles.

competitors.name: Hormel Foods Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Hormel is a smaller, branded-focused competitor (~$12B revenue vs. Tyson's ~$56B). Hormel's portfolio (Spam, Black Label, Skippy peanut butter) is more consumer-brand-anchored than Tyson's commodity-heavy mix. Hormel's Jardian acquisition (2021) expanded its plant-based protein exposure. Hormel's lower leverage and higher brand equity provide defensive positioning vs. Tyson's commodity-cycle exposure.

competitors.name: Sanderson Farms, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Sanderson Farms is the third-largest U.S. poultry processor (~8% market share). Sanderson is privately held (Cargill acquisition completed 2024); Cargill's integration of Sanderson into its poultry operations creates a new competitive dynamic. Sanderson's regional footprint (Southeast, Midwest) and lower-cost structure provide competitive pressure on Tyson's regional pricing.

competitors.name: Perdue Farms, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Perdue Farms is a privately held, family-controlled poultry processor (~7% U.S. market share). Perdue's brand equity (Perdue brand chicken) and vertical integration (genetics, feed, processing) create a differentiated competitive position vs. Tyson's commodity focus. Perdue's NAE positioning and premium pricing strategy limit direct price competition with Tyson.

competitors.name: Conagra Brands, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Conagra is a packaged-food competitor with significant meat-based product exposure (Slim Jim, Banquet, Marie Callender's). Conagra's reliance on Tyson and other meat suppliers for raw materials creates a customer-competitor dynamic. Conagra's 2024 margin pressure from input-cost inflation mirrors Tyson's upstream challenges.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.brainNodeRole: Compliance & Governance — disclosure and fiduciary oversight
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC oversees Tyson's 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, and proxy filings. Tyson's 2023 accounting restatement (inventory valuation) and subsequent internal-control remediation required SEC monitoring. Tyson's Tyson family voting-control structure (Class B shares) is subject to SEC proxy-disclosure rules and periodic review for fairness opinions.

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Agriculture
regulators.relationshipNote: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) conducts continuous inspection at all Tyson meat-processing plants. FSIS has authority to issue recalls, suspend operations, and impose civil penalties for food-safety violations. Tyson's 2024 salmonella recall (affecting ~35,000 lbs of chicken products) triggered FSIS investigation and remediation requirements. FSIS inspection findings are a leading indicator of operational stress.

regulators.name: Food and Drug Administration
regulators.relationshipNote: FDA oversees animal-drug approvals, food-labeling compliance, and dietary-supplement claims. FDA's 2023 guidance on antimicrobial-resistance reduction in animal agriculture directly impacts Tyson's NAE positioning and feed-additive costs. FDA's authority to issue recalls and import alerts creates tail risk for Tyson's supply chain.

regulators.name: Environmental Protection Agency
regulators.relationshipNote: EPA regulates Tyson's wastewater discharge (Clean Water Act), air emissions (Clean Air Act), and hazardous-waste management (RCRA). Tyson's large processing plants generate significant wastewater and air emissions; EPA enforcement actions have targeted Tyson for permit violations. Tyson's 2024 capital-expenditure plan includes $200M+ for environmental-compliance upgrades.

regulators.name: Occupational Safety and Health Administration
regulators.relationshipNote: OSHA regulates workplace safety at Tyson's processing plants. Tyson's injury rate (recordable incidents per 200,000 hours) has historically exceeded industry average; OSHA citations and penalties are recurring. Tyson's 2024 workplace-safety initiatives (automation, ergonomic redesign) aim to reduce injury rates and associated workers'-compensation costs.

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Justice
regulators.relationshipNote: DOJ Antitrust Division investigated Tyson and Pilgrim's Pride for alleged price-fixing in chicken (2019–2021). Investigation was closed without charges, but created reputational risk and operational scrutiny. DOJ continues to monitor poultry-industry consolidation; any future M&A by Tyson would face heightened antitrust review.

auditor.name: PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: PwC is Tyson's external independent auditor and issues annual audit opinion on 10-K financial statements and internal-control effectiveness. PwC's 2023 audit included remediation of prior-year inventory-valuation control deficiency. PwC's audit fees and scope are disclosed in Tyson's proxy statement; PwC also provides tax and advisory services (non-audit).

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan is Tyson's lead arranger and administrative agent on its $3.5B revolving credit facility (maturity 2028). JPMorgan also underwrite Tyson's bond issuances and provide treasury-management services. JPMorgan's relationship manager has direct access to Tyson's CFO and treasury team; covenant compliance and liquidity monitoring are continuous.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Corporation
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Bank of America is a syndicate member on Tyson's $3.5B revolving credit facility and participates in bond underwriting. BofA provides trade-finance services (letters of credit, supply-chain financing) for Tyson's commodity purchases and customer receivables.

capitalProviders.name: Tyson Family (Class B Shareholders)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: The Tyson family retains ~71% voting control via Class B shares (10 votes per share vs. 1 vote for Class A). John H. Tyson (founder's grandson) serves as Executive Vice President and CFO. Family control creates governance stability but limits institutional-investor influence on capital allocation and strategic direction. Family's long-term ownership horizon supports patient capital for cyclical downturns.

capitalProviders.name: Berkshire Hathaway Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Berkshire Hathaway holds ~5.1% of Tyson's Class A shares (as of 2024 10-K). Berkshire's investment signals confidence in Tyson's long-term value; however, Berkshire's recent reduction in equity holdings (2024) may signal concern about Tyson's leverage or commodity-cycle exposure. Berkshire's presence on the cap table provides implicit credit support.

executiveTeam.name: Donnie King
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Donnie King became CEO in 2021 after 30+ years at Tyson. King is a non-family operator with deep operational expertise in poultry and beef processing. King's strategic priorities include debt reduction, operational efficiency, and ESG compliance. King's compensation is tied to EBITDA and free-cash-flow targets; his tenure has coincided with P8 PIVOT phase classification.

executiveTeam.name: John R. Tyson
executiveTeam.role: Executive Vice President & Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: John R. Tyson (4th-generation family member) became CFO in 2022. John's background includes finance and operations roles within Tyson. Family + executive overlap creates governance complexity; John's voting power (via Class B shares) exceeds his operational authority. John's CFO tenure has focused on debt management and covenant compliance.

executiveTeam.name: Curt Covington
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Curt Covington is COO and oversees Tyson's three primary segments (poultry, beef, pork). Covington has 25+ years of operations experience in meat processing. Covington's operational initiatives include plant automation, supply-chain optimization, and safety improvements. Covington reports directly to CEO King.

executiveTeam.name: Shawn Kathleen Enevoldsen
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Shawn Enevoldsen is General Counsel and oversees legal, compliance, and regulatory affairs. Enevoldsen's portfolio includes USDA/FDA compliance, environmental permitting, and litigation management. Enevoldsen's team manages Tyson's response to regulatory investigations and class-action litigation.

marketSignals.name: Weekly Live-Animal Procurement Prices
marketSignals.relationshipNote: USDA reports weekly prices for live broilers, cattle, and hogs. Tyson's procurement costs track these indices with a 1–2 week lag. Spikes in live-animal prices (e.g., avian flu reducing broiler supply) create margin compression unless Tyson can pass through to customers within 30–60 days. Weekly price data is a real-time leading indicator of Tyson's gross-margin trajectory.

marketSignals.name: Retail Meat-Price Index (BLS)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes monthly retail prices for chicken, beef, and pork. Tyson's ability to pass through input-cost increases is measured by the lag between wholesale (Tyson's selling price) and retail (BLS index). Widening gap signals customer resistance to price increases; narrowing gap signals pricing power recovery.

matched.neuralRegionLabel: Striatal Projection Neurons (Cholinergic Interneuron–Mediated Phasic Gating Circuit)

patent.claimDirection: Automated interchange contingency-detection engine that monitors real-time network fee schedule feeds and triggers phasic merchant rate adjustment events within a configurable latency window, analogous to a synthetic TAN pause signal.
patent.noveltyAnchor: Dynamic phasic repricing trigger keyed to network fee effective-date metadata rather than manual billing cycle, with per-vertical interchange qualification scoring to minimize downgrade exposure.

programMatch: NSF Future of Work at the Human-Technology Frontier
grant.angle: Frame as adaptive financial infrastructure research: real-time payment cost contingency learning systems that reduce systemic merchant margin volatility, with the neural habit-rigidity model as the formal dynamical reference.

investment.thesis: Processors with demonstrated interchange optimization automation (real-time qualification scoring, dynamic rate-table patching) will sustain net revenue yield through network fee cycles; those without show lagged margin compression detectable 1-2 quarters post-schedule change—a timing arbitrage opportunity in Shift4 vs. peers.
investment.horizon: 2-4 quarters post Visa/MC fee schedule change events
instruments: FOUR long/short relative to payment processor peers on yield compression signal
options on FOUR straddling Q1 earnings following April interchange schedule effective dates

research.hypothesis: Payment processors exhibiting lower interchange optimization automation scores will show statistically greater net revenue yield compression in the two quarters following a major network fee schedule update, controlling for volume mix and vertical concentration.
research.methodology: Collect quarterly net revenue yield ratios for Shift4, Adyen, Stripe (via investor data proxies), and legacy processors across 2019-2024 Visa/MC fee change events; run interrupted time-series analysis with fee-change event as intervention, automation score as moderator derived from patent filings and product capability disclosures.

L-DOPA augmentation (restoring dopaminergic D2 modulation of TAN pause probability)
Deep brain stimulation of striatum (exogenous phasic interruption of tonic cholinergic suppression)
